explanation: The passage states: 'A green roof is created by covering part or all of a building's roof with soil and plants.' The statement says the same thing in different words.

passage: Rooftop gardens, sometimes called green roofs, are becoming a familiar sight in several large cities. A green roof is created by covering part or all of a building's roof with soil and plants. Supporters argue that they cool the surrounding air: plants release water vapour through their leaves, a process known as transpiration, which lowers the temperature of the air above the roof. A study carried out in Chicago in 2019 compared two neighbouring office buildings, one with a green roof and one with a conventional dark roof. On the hottest summer days, the surface of the green roof was up to 30 degrees cooler than the conventional roof. The researchers also recorded lower indoor temperatures in the building below the green roof, which reduced the need for air conditioning during the afternoon. However, installing a green roof is expensive, and the building must be strong enough to support the extra weight of soil and water. For this reason, engineers recommend a structural survey before any installation begins.
source: Original practice passage authored for Unschool Academy; True/False/Not Given rules per the official IELTS Reading test format (ielts.org — British Council / IDP / Cambridge English)

passage: Scientists have long suspected a link between sleep and memory, and recent experiments have strengthened this view. In a 2021 study at a German university, two groups of students were asked to memorise a list of 40 pairs of words. One group then slept for eight hours, while the other stayed awake and went about its normal day. When both groups were tested the following evening, the group that had slept remembered an average of 28 word pairs, compared with 21 for the group that had stayed awake. The researchers concluded that sleep helps the brain to organise and store new information. Interestingly, the benefit was greatest for the word pairs that students had found most difficult during the learning session. The team now plans to investigate whether shorter naps produce a similar effect, although no results have been published yet.
source: Original practice passage authored for Unschool Academy; True/False/Not Given rules per the official IELTS Reading test format (ielts.org — British Council / IDP / Cambridge English)

explanation: The passage says: 'most wild bee species are solitary' — solitary means living alone, not in colonies. The statement agrees.

passage: Wild bees are among the most effective pollinators of crops and wildflowers, yet their numbers have fallen sharply in many regions. Unlike honeybees, which live in large managed colonies, most wild bee species are solitary, with each female building her own nest. Researchers believe the main cause of the decline is the loss of flower-rich habitats: as meadows are converted to farmland or housing, bees struggle to find enough food through the spring and summer. Pesticides are also thought to play a role, although the evidence is less clear. In Britain, a nationwide survey found that the ranges of one-third of wild bee species shrank between 1980 and 2010. Conservation groups now encourage gardeners to plant native wildflowers and to leave small areas of bare ground, where many solitary bees prefer to nest.
source: Original practice passage authored for Unschool Academy; True/False/Not Given rules per the official IELTS Reading test format (ielts.org — British Council / IDP / Cambridge English)

passage: Each year, an estimated eight million tonnes of plastic waste enter the world's oceans, where currents gather much of it into vast rotating patches of debris. In 2018, a Dutch non-profit organisation launched a floating barrier designed to collect this plastic. The 600-metre-long barrier uses the ocean's own currents to funnel floating debris towards a central collection point, from where ships periodically remove it. During its first year of operation, the system collected over 100,000 kilograms of plastic, although its founders admit this is a tiny fraction of the total. Critics argue that the barrier may also trap marine animals, and that preventing plastic from entering the sea in the first place would be more effective. The organisation has announced plans to expand the system, but has not said how the expansion will be funded.

explanation: The passage opens: 'The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes.' The statement agrees.
hint: Was it 'a single road' or 'a network'? Check the first sentence.
passage: The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes linking China with the Mediterranean world for more than 1,500 years. Caravans carried silk, spices, and precious stones westward, while glass, wool, and gold travelled east. Few merchants completed the entire journey; instead, goods changed hands many times at busy market towns along the way. The routes also carried ideas: Buddhism spread from India to China along these paths, and papermaking technology eventually reached Europe the same way. Trade declined in the 1400s, partly because sea routes offered a faster and cheaper way to move goods. Along with goods, the routes carried new foods, animals, and craft techniques in both directions, quietly changing diets and workshops in distant lands. Today, several countries are investing in new rail and road links across Central Asia, which some commentators have nicknamed the 'New Silk Road'. Whether these modern routes will reshape trade as profoundly as the old ones remains to be seen.
source: Original practice passage authored for Unschool Academy; True/False/Not Given rules per the official IELTS Reading test format (ielts.org — British Council / IDP / Cambridge English)

passage: Vertical farming — growing crops in stacked layers inside buildings — promises to produce food close to where it is eaten. Because the plants grow indoors under LED lights, farmers can control temperature, humidity, and light precisely, and harvests are possible all year round. The method uses far less water than traditional farming, since water is recycled through the system rather than lost to the soil. At present, however, vertical farms mostly grow leafy greens and herbs; crops such as wheat and rice, which need large areas and long growing seasons, remain uneconomical to produce this way. The electricity needed for lighting is another concern, although some operators now run their farms on renewable energy. Supporters predict that as LED technology improves and energy costs fall, a wider range of crops will become viable.

passage: Vertical farming — growing crops in stacked layers inside buildings — promises to produce food close to where it is eaten. Because the plants grow indoors under LED lights, farmers can control temperature, humidity, and light precisely, and harvests are possible all year round. The method uses far less water than traditional farming, since water is recycled through the system rather than lost to the soil. At present, however, vertical farms mostly grow leafy greens and herbs; crops such as wheat and rice, which need large areas and long growing seasons, remain uneconomical to produce this way. The electricity needed for lighting is another concern, although some operators now run their farms on renewable energy. Supporters predict that as LED technology improves and energy costs fall, a wider range of crops will become viable.
